findings.title: fetch_if_missing reports complete for a range wider than previously fetched coverage (range-widening honesty bug)
findings.evidence: service.py:334-352 (_never compares requested range with stored coverage_), service.py:268-269 (elif selected: status=complete), repository.py:360-406 (coverage observation stores no requested range/boundary). Reproduced by reviewer: fresh root, request A from=2025-01-01 -> complete with 6 periods (terminal=period_boundary); request B from=2016-01-01 -> status=complete, http=0, only 10 of 36 periods (2024-03-31..2026-06-30) served while advertised_report_count=36.
findings.recommendation: Persist the fetched range/boundary (e.g. fetched_from) in financial_statement_coverage; in _needs_fetch treat requests extending beyond the stored boundary as missing (refetch) or return partial with a named gap (range_not_covered); add a narrow-then-wide regression test.

findings.title: Row-bound truncation is silent: continuation/truncated dropped and fields filter not exposed in the request contract
findings.evidence: service.py:279-290 calls query_statement_rows(max_rows=20000) but never reads query['continuation']/['truncated'] computed at repository.py:321-331; contracts.py:150-157 allowed request fields contain no fields/continuation/max_rows; repository.py:456-561 readonly query returns continuation:null only. Latent for CN A-shares (max ~6k rows/table << 20000) but truncation would stay status=complete with no resume token.
findings.recommendation: Pass continuation/truncated through the response (force partial when truncated), or add fields/continuation to financial-statements-request/1; document the default row/byte bound.

findings.title: FF mislabels CWP request_error as upstream_error with retryable=true
findings.evidence: ff/scripts/ff_financial_statements.py:143-148 maps any nonzero child exit to code=upstream_error and discards the child's stdout error envelope. Reviewer run: fetch_statements.py with period_end_from>period_end_to -> exit 2 (correct) but envelope status=upstream_error, retryable=true, producer_exit_code=2 while CWP itself printed status=request_error.
findings.recommendation: On exit 2 parse the child stdout envelope and propagate status=request_error/config_error with retryable=false (keep producer_exit_code), or validate period ordering on the FF side first.

findings.title: Top-level status 'unavailable' is unreachable; total provider failure reported as partial
findings.evidence: service.py:169-177 _overall_status only yields complete/not_found/partial. Reviewer run: fresh root + broken fixture root -> all three statements unavailable(provider_unavailable/http_error) yet response.status=partial.
findings.recommendation: Return top-level unavailable when every statement is unavailable; add a test.

findings.title: Uncommitted code changes sit on top of the reviewed commit in the CWP workspace
findings.evidence: git status in company-wiki-w19-sina-statements: M src/company_wiki/source_catalog/financial_statements/service.py, M tests/financial_statements/test_service_contracts.py (adds _apply_identity_gap / ambiguous-identity candidates + 1 test, not part of e583904d). Reviewer overlay run of e583904d + these two files: 92 passed.
findings.recommendation: Before handoff either commit the change and submit the diff for supplemental independent review (updating the bound SHA) or revert it; record the final reviewed commit in handoff.json per COMMON section 4.

findings.title: Per-report field is captured_at while the card's frozen per-report list says retrieved_at
findings.evidence: Card section 3.2 per-report field list includes retrieved_at; service.py:468-511 emits captured_at per report (response-level retrieved_at exists at service.py:111).
findings.recommendation: Add a retrieved_at alias per report or document the naming deviation in the handoff interface section (captured_at better matches card section 5 capture-time semantics).

findings.title: balance_sheet instant semantics are not machine-readable
findings.evidence: schema.py:25-27 period_kind CHECK allows only annual/semi_annual/q1/q3; no 'instant' anywhere in the package; test_normalize.py::test_balance_sheet_period_kind_and_statement_semantics asserts period_kind=='semi_annual' and relies on statement_type to convey instant semantics; period_start is always null.
findings.recommendation: Document the encoding contract in the handoff or add an explicit value_basis=instant|duration field without breaking the existing CHECK.

findings.title: No replay-from-committed-SourceRef path after a normalization failure
findings.evidence: service.py:435 normalizes only after the original is committed; a NormalizeProtocolError propagates to cli.py:171-176 (fatal exit 1) with no coverage observation recorded, so the next fetch_if_missing re-networks (bytes dedup, HTTP repeats). Only --fixture-root replay exists (cli.py:56-84), which replays the fixture root, not catalog originals.
findings.recommendation: Add an entry that re-normalizes/publishes from an already committed source_id with zero network, plus a test for 'bad payload committed then replayed offline'.

findings.title: Fixture replay mode reports response_bytes=0, so offline receipts cannot evidence byte accounting or the max_bytes budget
findings.evidence: Reviewer runs: usage.response_bytes=0 with http_requests=15. Minimal repro: BudgetedHTTPTransport(MockTransport(handler)) + response.content -> budget.response_bytes_used=0 because httpx short-circuits read() for content= responses (bytes never traverse the metering stream). Production path (real HTTPTransport streaming) meters correctly.
findings.recommendation: Meter bytes inside the replay transport or explicitly document that offline runs do not account bytes; never cite offline response_bytes as real byte evidence in handoff.
